subject: Graceful migration: credit scenarios & ops checklist
messages:
From: Tom Parks <tom.parks@runway.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Runway Procurement <procurement@runway.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick question on matching AtlasCore + migration support

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for taking the time last week on the call. Runway is evaluating a move off AtlasCore and we need two things to make the switch viable for our team: a price/packaging alignment that gets within ~10% of our current committed unit cost, and a clear migration credit/onboarding schedule to offset ramp costs.

Two quick asks to get us started:
1) Can you provide a few concrete credit scenarios (e.g., month-by-month offsets or a one-time migration rebate) tied to a 12-18 month committed path?
2) Ops: what handoffs and SLOs should we expect during the first 90 days (tech onboarding, rate limits, elevated support)?

Our current contract: AtlasCore, committed 48M tokens/month, multi-region, 99.9% uptime SLA. We need numbers we can take to our procurement team this week.

If helpful Im happy to share the AtlasCore redline and a summary of their effective unit-rate.

Best,
Tom
Tom Parks
Head of Platform
Runway AI

Tom,

Really appreciate the clear asks — we can absolutely put together a short set of scenarios you can take to procurement this week. Ive looped in Jordan (commercial) for the credit math and Laura (customer ops) for the 90-day onboarding checklist.

High-level thought: we generally avoid one-off large cash buyouts; instead we propose staged migration credits tied to observed usage in months 1-4 plus a technical onboarding credit that covers hands-on migration support (scripts, prefix caching, and a dedicated migration runbook). That gives you a predictable dollar bridge while aligning incentives.

Ill share an editable worksheet (attached) with three scenarios and an ops checklist by EOD PT. Can you confirm: 1) whether the committed token baseline you mentioned is current usage or a target commitment if you switch? and 2) any specific compliance or FedRAMP-like requirements we should flag up front?

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on matching AtlasCore + migration support (internal)

Team — draft numbers below, conservative rounding. Im proposing three scenarios we can present: Conservative, Balanced, and Accelerated. All assume a 12-month commitment from Runway and a migration onboarding package from our Customer Ops SKU pool.

1) Conservative (minimal upfront):
   - Migration credit: 2 months of equivalent committed units (applied as credits over first 3 invoices)
   - Effective unit-rate gap covered: ~6% for first 6 months
   - No prepaid; standard onboarding (self-service + office hours)

2) Balanced (our standard competitive match):
   - Migration credit: 3 months of committed units + $25k technical onboarding credit
   - Effective unit-rate gap covered: ~9–11% during 0–6 months
   - 6-months elevated support (priority queue + 4 on-call migration sessions)

3) Accelerated (move quickly / low friction):
   - Migration credit: 5 months of committed units + $60k onboarding & hands-on migration (dedicated eng time)
   - Effective unit-rate gap covered: ~14–16% first 6 months
   - 90-day SLA uplift guarantees for critical endpoints (on-call post-migration)

Ops checklist notes for Laura: please draft the 90-day runbook items we should commit to in the term sheet — prefer a short, prescriptive list (kickoff, data ingress, perf validation, rollback gates, post-mortem). Also confirm what we can realistically guarantee for multi-region failover in month 1 vs month 3.

If we need to lean more on credits vs. price cuts, recommend the Balanced option as our middle ground — its defensible vs procurement and preserves list pricing.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Head of Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference

Tom —

Thanks again for the details. Based on our internal review, attached is a compact term sheet outlining the Balanced migration path (recommended) and the Conservative/Accelerated alternatives for your procurement review. Quick summary below so you can forward it into your internal packet: 

Balanced (recommended) — headline
• Migration credit: 3 months of committed units applied as credits over first 3 invoices
• $25k technical onboarding credit (hands-on sessions + runbook delivery)
• 6 months elevated support: priority queue, 4 migration sessions, monthly performance call
• Price match target: within 10% of AtlasCore effective unit-rate for months 1–6

Ops & timelines (90 days):
• Week 0: Kickoff + access & network connectivity checks
• Week 1–3: Data sync and prefix caching configuration; perf baseline tests
• Week 4–8: Pilot traffic ramp, SLA validation, tuning tweaks
• Week 9–12: Cutover window, final validation, rollback window and post-mortem

Next steps:
1) If this looks reasonable Ill schedule a 30-min procurement alignment call with Jordan and our legal rep.
2) We can bake the exact credit math into a simple amendment once Runway confirms commitment length/target baseline.

Ive attached a short term sheet (runway-migration-term-sheet.pdf) and the editable worksheet we mentioned. If youd like, we can also run a sample cost-reconciliation with your AtlasCore effective rate — just share the summary.

Best,
